instructions: In a bowl, whisk 3 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, 3 cloves of the garlic (minced), 2 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper.
Cut the chicken thighs into 1 1/2-inch chunks and toss them in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to overnight if you want deeper flavor).
While the chicken marinates, make the tzatziki: grate the cucumber, squeeze out as much water as you can with your hands or a towel, or the sauce will be watery.

Mix the grated cucumber with the Greek yogurt, the last garlic clove (grated), the juice of the remaining lemon, 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt and 1 tbsp chopped fresh dill. Taste and add more salt or lemon if it's flat. Refrigerate until serving.
Cut the bell pepper and red onion into chunks about the same size as the chicken. Toss them with the remaining 1/2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, alternating with pieces of pepper and onion, leaving a little room between pieces so everything cooks evenly.
Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill to high. Lay the skewers down and leave them alone for 3-4 minutes until the underside is well charred and releases easily from the grates.
Flip and grill the other side for another 3-4 minutes, until charred and the chicken reaches 165°F in the center. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece. It's done when there's no pink left.
While the chicken rests for a couple of minutes, warm the pita on the grill or in a dry pan for 20-30 seconds per side, until soft and lightly toasted in spots.
Taste the tzatziki one more time. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lemon.
Serve the skewers with the warm pita and the tzatziki, with extra fresh dill scattered over the top.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the chicken at least 30 minutes ahead; can be done the night before for deeper flavor.

My Greek Dish's method: chicken breast is cut into chunks and marinated in extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, chopped garlic, and dried oregano, with a minimum marinade time of about 30 minutes in the fridge (longer preferred for deeper flavor). Chicken pieces are threaded loosely onto skewers so they cook evenly, optionally alternated with chunks of red/green bell pepper and red onion cut to the same size, oiled and seasoned with salt and pepper. Skewers are grilled at high heat until nicely charred and cooked through, with doneness checked via internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) to keep the meat juicy rather than dry. The finished souvlaki is served with homemade tzatziki sauce and warm pita bread, in the traditional Greek street-food style, with tzatziki and pita treated as essential accompaniments rather than optional sides.
